p: Complete: Wind and water are two ___ forces.
ex: Wind and water exist in nature, so they are natural forces.

p: Complete: Wind and water can be ___ to us.
ex: Wind and water can help us and can harm us: helpful and harmful.

p: Which of these is HELPFUL water?
ex: Helpful water: water the plants, water to make energy. A tsunami and floods are harmful.

p: Which of these is HELPFUL wind?
ex: Helpful wind: makes energy and spreads the seeds. Tornadoes and strong winds are harmful.

p: Which of these is HARMFUL water?
ex: Harmful water: a tsunami, heavy rain and floods. Energy and plants are helpful uses.

p: Which of these is HARMFUL wind?
ex: Harmful wind: a tornado and strong winds. Seeds and energy are helpful uses.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: A tsunami is a giant wave of water. It is harmful.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: Heavy rain can make floods. The water covers streets and cars. It is harmful.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: A tornado is wind that spins in a tall funnel. It is harmful.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: These strong winds bend the trees and blow the leaves. They are harmful.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: Watering the plants is on the helpful list. Water helps plants live.

p: What is this? Helpful or harmful?
ex: A dam uses moving water to make energy. It is helpful.

p: Which natural force turns these blades?
ex: Wind turns the blades of a turbine. Wind is the force here.

p: Which natural force spreads these seeds?
ex: The seeds float in the air. Wind spreads the seeds, and that is helpful.

p: Which natural force is this?
ex: A tornado is spinning wind. So it is the force of wind.

p: Which natural force is this?
ex: A tsunami is a giant wave. So it is the force of water.

p: What do these wind turbines make?
ex: Wind turns the turbines, and the turbines make electricity.

p: Which natural forces can make energy?
ex: The slide shows water to make energy and wind to make energy. So both.

p: Complete: Wind is ___ in motion.
ex: Wind is air in motion. Moving air is wind.

p: Wind can be soft or strong. Which one is SOFT wind?
ex: A gentle breeze is soft wind. A mighty gust is strong wind.

p: You blow bubbles. What does your breath make?
ex: Wind is air in motion. Blowing bubbles moves air, so it makes wind.

p: Which natural force makes a kite fly?
ex: A kite flies with the wind. Moving air holds it up.

p: Wind moves sand. What can it make?
ex: Wind moves sand and makes dunes. Water makes valleys and canyons.

p: Wind and sand wear rock. What can they make?
ex: Wind and sand wear rock and make arches. Valleys come from water.

p: Complete: Water is always ___.
ex: Water is always moving. It can be helpful or harmful.

p: Complete: Rivers flow ___.
ex: Rivers flow downhill. Water moves from high places to low places.

p: Moving water wears rock. What can it make?
ex: Water wears rock and makes valleys and canyons. Wind makes dunes and arches.

p: Rain falls on the ground. What can it carry away?
ex: Rain is moving water. It can carry soil away from the ground.

p: A boat has a big sail. Which natural force fills the sail?
ex: Sailing uses wind. Wind fills the sail and moves the boat.

p: A dam uses moving water. What does it make?
ex: Dams use moving water to make electricity. This is called hydroelectricity.

p: How do farmers use water?
ex: Farmers use water to water their fields. Wind spreads seeds and makes dunes.

p: We drink with it. We cook with it. We wash with it. Which natural force is it?
ex: We use water for drinking, cooking and washing.

p: Ships and boats travel on...
ex: Boats and ships use water to travel. Water carries them.

p: Complete: Rivers are home to...
ex: Rivers are home to fish and frogs. They live in and near the water.

p: Complete: We need to protect our...
ex: Wind is moving air, and water is the other force. We need to protect both.

p: Complete: The ___ spreads the seeds.
ex: Wind is the natural force that spreads the seeds. A window is part of a house.

p: How does a fish move?
ex: A fish lives in the water and moves by swimming. A fish swims.

p: Which animal flies?
ex: To fly is to move through the air. A bird flies.

p: A monkey goes up a tree. How does it move?
ex: A monkey goes up a tree with its hands and feet. It climbs.

p: How does a dog move?
ex: A dog moves on four legs. A dog walks and runs.

p: Which animal jumps?
ex: A kangaroo moves by jumping. It uses its strong back legs.

p: How does a frog move on land?
ex: A frog and a kangaroo move the same way. They jump.

p: A snake has no legs. How does it move on the ground?
ex: A snake has no legs. It stays low and crawls on the ground.

p: A snake moves smoothly along the ground. Which word fits?
ex: To slide is to move smoothly along a surface. A snake slides on the ground.

p: I go up a tree. I use my body. I…
ex: Climb is a body movement. We climb to go up a tree.

p: I move in the pool with my whole body. I…
ex: Swim is a body movement. We swim in the water, like a fish.

p: I ___ on a chair.
ex: Sit is a body movement. We sit on a chair.

p: My legs and feet take me to the door. I…
ex: Walk is a body movement. We use our legs and feet to walk.

p: Which one is on the list of body movements?
ex: Body list: swim, climb, play, walk, pick, sit. Play is on it.

p: Body movements: swim, climb, play, walk, sit and…
ex: Body list: swim, climb, play, walk, pick, sit. Pick is on it.

p: I use my hand and a pencil. I…
ex: Write is a hand movement. We hold a pencil and write.

p: I show a place on the map with my finger. I…
ex: Point is a hand movement. We point with a finger to show a place.

p: My hand closes fast around the ball. I…
ex: Grab is a hand movement. The hand closes and holds the ball.

p: My hands move the box up. I…
ex: Lift is a hand movement. Hands move a thing up.

p: My fingers feel the soft cat. I…
ex: Touch is a hand movement. We touch things with our fingers.

p: Which one is on the list of hand movements?
ex: Hand list: touch, lift, point, write, grab, push. Push is on it.
